meta.title: Build Your Onboarding
meta.subtitle: Sandbox · Craft & Build
meta.briefing: Your first-90-days handbook, as a claim you work. Mine the facts for materials, craft each step of the plan, and watch your onboarding rise out of the ground.

sourceElement.label: Your Manager
sourceElement.description: Nobody remembers a handbook. You remember what you built. Go dig up the facts and assemble the thing.

sourceElement.label: Who owns what
sourceElement.description: Four teams own the product surface: platform, growth, billing, and support. Escalations route by surface, not by seniority.

sourceElement.label: Deploy cadence
sourceElement.description: Production ships twice daily at 10:00 and 16:00. Anything outside that window needs an incident ticket.

sourceElement.label: On-call rotation
sourceElement.description: One week per engineer per quarter, handover every Monday at 11:00 with a written summary.

sourceElement.label: Review standard
sourceElement.description: Two approvals for anything touching billing or auth; one approval everywhere else.

sourceElement.label: The customer promise
sourceElement.description: 99.9% uptime and a four-hour first response on paid plans — every technical decision ladders up to those two numbers.

sourceElement.label: Internal glossary
sourceElement.description: "Surface" means a product area. "Lane" means a delivery team. "Freeze" means no deploys, not no work.

sourceElement.label: The tool chain
sourceElement.description: Tickets in Linear, docs in Notion, incidents in PagerDuty, everything else in the repo.

sourceElement.label: Decision records
sourceElement.description: Every architectural decision gets a one-page record with the alternatives that were rejected and why.

sourceElement.label: Meeting rhythm
sourceElement.description: Standup Monday and Thursday, review on Friday, and nothing else on the calendar by default.

sourceElement.label: Stand up your dev environment
sourceElement.description: Clone, seed, and get the test suite green locally before touching anything shared.

sourceElement.label: Ship a first pull request
sourceElement.description: Something small and real in week one — a doc fix counts, a no-op does not.

sourceElement.label: Shadow an on-call week
sourceElement.description: Sit the rotation with someone experienced before you carry the pager yourself.

sourceElement.label: Meet all four surface owners
sourceElement.description: A 30-minute conversation with each owner, with one written takeaway per meeting.

sourceElement.label: Take ownership of one surface
sourceElement.description: By day 60 you should be the person others ask about one specific area.

sourceElement.label: Write your first decision record
sourceElement.description: Pick something you changed and document why, including what you chose not to do.

sourceElement.label: The silent blocker
sourceElement.description: Being stuck for more than half a day without asking costs the team more than the interruption would.

sourceElement.label: First-month scope creep
sourceElement.description: Saying yes to everything in month one is how new hires end up owning nothing by month three.

sourceElement.label: First 30 days
sourceElement.description: Environment running, first PR shipped, and every surface owner met.

sourceElement.label: First 90 days
sourceElement.description: On-call shadowed, one surface owned, and a decision record written.
